annotations.text:
(Recommended) Table A · axis: mobile stacking.
Why: at 375 the four live tables split two ways. table-tblc is the only one that already stacks to data-label cards, and it is the only one of the four where every cell is fully readable with no horizontal scroll: table-others-375 clips the whole "Best for" column off the right edge of the screen, and table-mvf-375 fits only by breaking cells to one or two words per line, so "Often a touch more talkative and a bolder mimic" reads down five lines. Stacking every row into a card reproduces the one pattern that already works here, needs no JavaScript, and keeps all three or four cells of a row visible at once.
Trade-off: it is the tallest mobile answer of the three (Congo vs Timneh runs about 3,400px), so side-by-side comparison becomes vertical scrolling instead of a glance.

Table B · axis: mobile disclosure.
Why: table-cmp is the one live table that already ships a Congo/Timneh tab toggle, and table-cmp-375 is readable at 375 where its untabbed siblings are not, so the pattern is proven on this site rather than borrowed. Tablet and desktop keep the classic table with the row-label column pinned by position:sticky so it stays on screen while the value columns move, with overflow-x as the secondary affordance only.
Trade-off: one column at a time means a buyer cannot weigh male against female, or Congo against Timneh, without a tap, and the toggle needs JavaScript, so with scripts off the page falls back to the scrolling table the breeder rejected.

Table C · axis: verdict emphasis.
Why: three of the four tables already carry a verdict the classic layout buries in the last column. Congo vs Timneh has an Edge column that names Timneh on three rows, Grey vs Other Species tints the African Grey row, and Rearing Paths badges hand-raised as the Top pick. The verdict card lifts that call into a forest strip under the two mini-columns, and the zebra ledger at tablet and desktop tints only the cells the source table actually marks.
Trade-off: Male vs Female marks no winner at all, so its cards carry no strip and the variation buys nothing on that table, and it is the tallest mobile stack of the three at Congo vs Timneh, about 3,700px.

table-mvf · live on / (homepage), section 11b, under the heading "Should You Choose a Male or Female African Grey?". In table-mvf-375 and in the breeder's screenshot "what buyers ask about.png", three text columns are squeezed into 375 and the cells break to one or two words a line. The "Telling them apart" row spans both value columns and has no per-column answer, so any variation has to handle it as a full-width note.

table-others · live on / (homepage), section 11c, under the heading "How Does an African Grey Compare to a Macaw, Cockatoo, or Amazon?". This is the worst of the four on a phone: in table-others-375 and in the breeder's screenshot "african vs otherrs table.png" the fourth column, "Best for", is cut off at the right edge, so the reader never sees the answer the row exists to give. The African Grey row is the only one the source tints.

table-cmp · live on /congo-vs-timneh-african-grey/, section S6, under the heading "How Do Congo and Timneh Greys Compare Side-by-Side?". Twelve rows and four columns, the widest of the four, and the only one with a named verdict column (Edge). Its mobile answer is already a Congo/Timneh tab toggle, which is why table-cmp-375 reads cleanly while its siblings do not; the breeder's screenshot "table e desktop.png" is the desktop state.

table-tblc · live on /hand-raised-african-grey-parrot-for-sale/, section 02, under the heading "The Three Rearing Paths, Side by Side". It already stacks to data-label cards at 375 and is the one table of the four with no readability defect, so it sits here as the control; the breeder's screenshot "handraised table.png" is the desktop state. Its "Top pick" badge on hand-raised is the only explicit winner mark among the four.
